items.text: Stripe PaymentIntents is the processor for card payments in the November release
November scope is cards and saved cards; Apple Pay and wallets later
No generic payment-provider interface now; keep the internal payment model clean enough to add another processor later
Every payment creation request needs an idempotency key persisted with the payment record
Postgres is the source of truth for payment idempotency with a unique constraint; idempotency key unique per merchant payment request
Same key and merchant returns the original result; same key with a different request body is rejected
Backend recognizes duplicate requests; cannot rely on the frontend disabling the button
Webhook is the authoritative asynchronous confirmation; show success immediately if the synchronous response confirms, webhook still reconciles
Internal payment state machine with the raw processor status stored separately
API exposes a stable internal response, not the Stripe object, to the frontend
No card details or client secrets in logs; log PaymentIntent ID and internal payment ID
Verify Stripe webhook signatures before processing
Webhooks persisted to Postgres and processed asynchronously through the existing SQS infrastructure; no new Kafka cluster
GET /payments/{id} so the order page can fetch payment status
Metrics for webhook failures, payment creation failures, processing latency and reconciliation lag
Webhook backlog alert starts at ten minutes, adjusted after production data
Refunds and partial captures are out of scope for November
Saved cards required; store Stripe customer and payment method identifiers, no raw card data
All payment APIs require authenticated users with ownership-based authorization checks
Tenant isolation non-negotiable: authorization checks in the service layer plus cross-tenant access tests; no full RLS before November
No separate payment microservice; payments as an isolated module inside the checkout service
New checkout flow behind a feature flag with the old flow as fallback, starting at 1% rollout
Roll back if payment creation success rate, webhook processing latency or checkout conversion regress materially
Store every webhook event for audit trail and replay
Unique constraint on the Stripe event ID so retried webhooks are not processed twice
Basic daily reconciliation job in scope; full real-time reconciliation not
Pin the Stripe API version for this release
Document idempotency key behaviour
Implement the SQS webhook consumer
Add GET /payment-methods and associate the Stripe customer with the user account
Audit the existing checkout state transitions
Implement the daily reconciliation job
Document the API contract and state machine
Document the Stripe integration and webhook event mappings
Propose the rollout thresholds and monitoring alerts
Coordinate with compliance on webhook retention
What happens when Stripe is unavailable for ten minutes
A request timeout does not mean the payment failed
Blindly retrying create-payment could create a second PaymentIntent
If Redis is flushed, duplicate payments could be created
Stripe captures the payment but the database write fails, so we think it failed
Eventual webhook reconciliation can leave the order stuck in pending
Existing code assumes every successful payment is immediately final, which breaks with asynchronous processing
Webhooks can be delayed or lost
An unexpected Stripe API version change could break responses
Adyen would add a lot of work now
Actual rollout and rollback thresholds are an open item
Webhook event retention period, until compliance confirms
